seam.signature: runWithInput(options, in, out, opener, startInput, afterRecoveryReport ...func())
seam.behavior: An optional first callback is called synchronously on the actual session goroutine immediately after recovery reportWaiting Stop succeeds through await, before pendingControl inspection and epoch-owned finalization. It runs outside mailbox locks. Omitted or nil callback does nothing. Callback may be invoked for each successful recovery report, so the test should gate only its intended first recovery.
seam.minimality: One optional argument on the existing internal entry; no new wrapper, dependency structure, public API, environment hook, fake controller, or copied recovery logic. Public Run and runWithTranscript signatures and default callers unchanged; existing runWithInput calls compile unchanged.
seam.preserved_fix: Clear timer/cancelAt and enable admission only with pendingControl nil and ownership of captured recovery epoch. A newer real mailbox control causes failed ownership, retains the original first deadline, and continues to consume/process controls. cancelWait remains three seconds.

next_test_writer_use: Extend only the test fixture to forward the optional callback to its existing runWithInput call; keep default fixture calls unchanged.

Use existing reporter Stop after-commit barrier to hold actual first recovery. Keep superseding controls absent until report completion has selected successfully; release that reporter and await the new callback's entered channel.

While callback holds the session goroutine, inject the superseding interrupt using emit captured from the actual inputStarter. Do not invoke ordinary admit for this control. Its real mailbox insertion advances epoch; pendingControl remains nil because the controller is parked after await and has not consumed that control.

Release callback to resume the actual pendingControl/ifCurrent finalization; block the subsequent protected input_control Sync using existing recordBarrier. Assert failure and owned termination obey the original first-control three-second deadline, rather than a fresh deadline after recovery. Use channel ordering and existing bounded receipts; no randomized select/scheduling assumptions. The callback itself adds no production timing behavior when omitted.
